stages.title: Design the two-tier trust hierarchy
stages.detail: The root establishes trust. The subordinate, also called the issuing CA in this design, handles approved end-entity certificates. Keeping these roles separate protects the root from daily network exposure.

stages.title: Configure the offline Root CA
stages.detail: Treat root installation as a controlled event. Its private key is the highest-value secret in the hierarchy, and its configuration shapes the subordinate certificate it will sign.

stages.title: Create the issuing CA request
stages.detail: Prepare the online issuing server, but keep issuance paused until its CA certificate has been signed and installed. The request carries the public key; the private key stays protected on the issuing system or its approved key provider.

stages.title: Sign through the offline ceremony
stages.detail: A signing ceremony connects an approved request to an approved CA identity. A matching filename alone is not proof that the root should trust the request.

stages.title: Activate the issuing CA and distribute trust
stages.detail: A signed certificate is not yet a working CA. Install it, start Certificate Services, set the AIA and CDP locations every issued certificate will carry, and distribute the approved root through managed domain policy.

stages.title: Build the pki.sbd.test publication site
stages.detail: Every certificate the issuing CA has signed carries the pki.sbd.test URLs inside it. This lesson gives those URLs a real home: a small web site on SBD-PKI-MGMT01 serving certificates and revocation lists to the whole network.

stages.title: Publish the trust data at its advertised URLs
stages.detail: A publication site is only correct when the filenames it serves match the URLs the certificates already carry. Copy the current certificates and CRLs into place, wire the issuing CA to keep them fresh, and prove retrieval from a client that has never cached anything.

stages.title: Separate template administration
stages.detail: Certificate templates are directory objects, and whoever edits them decides what the PKI will sign. Give that power its own seat — SBD-PKI-MGMT01 — with named administrators, instead of leaving it wherever a CA console happens to be open.

stages.title: Publish the first working templates
stages.detail: The default template set is a menu, not a deployment. Duplicate the three templates this network actually needs — domain controller, computer and server authentication — set their cryptography deliberately, and publish only those.

stages.title: Validate enrollment, revocation, and recovery
stages.detail: Finish the way relying systems see it: both domain controllers and a pilot machine enroll on their own, validate against the live publication site, and reject a certificate you revoke — then the closing scans record what this course changed and close course 1.4's domain controller certificate finding.

title: Configure the two-tier PKI
subtitle: Offline root, issuing CA, pki.sbd.test publication & templates
description: Build a complete two-tier public key infrastructure: an offline standalone Root CA and an enterprise issuing CA, signed through a controlled ceremony, with trust data served from pki.sbd.test at the exact embedded URLs, template administration on its own seat, certificates for both domain controllers, and enrollment and revocation proven end to end.
outcomes: Design the CA hierarchy and its publication dependencies.
Configure the offline root and sign an issuing CA request through controlled media transfer.
Publish certificates and CRLs at the exact URLs issued certificates carry, from pki.sbd.test.
Move template administration to a delegated seat, give both domain controllers their certificates, and prove autoenrollment and revocation end to end.
outcomeSummary: An offline root, a working issuing CA, and trust data served at exactly the URLs every certificate carries.
